We have forgiven their shortcomings.

data.definition: To abandon or renounce completely.
examples: He forsakes worldly ambitions.
She forsook her career for family.
They have forsaken their old habits.

data.definition: To formally renounce or give up.
examples: He forswears alcohol for good.
She forswore violence in protest.
Monks have forsworn luxury items.

data.definition: To turn into ice or harden with cold.
examples: Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius.
The lake froze over last winter.
The ice cream has frozen hard.

data.definition: To deny or contradict facts.
examples: No one gainsays facts presented.
She gainsaid his claims in court.
His integrity cannot be gainsaid.

data.definition: To receive, obtain, or become.
examples: She gets good grades in school.
He got a new job last month.
They have gotten many presents.

data.definition: To have a harmonious, friendly relationship with someone.
data.grammar_rule: Three-part inseparable phrasal verb. Cannot split 'along with'.
examples: Do you get along with your new room-mate?
He gets along well with all his colleagues.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I get along my boss. ➔ ✅ I get along with my boss.

data.definition: To escape punishment or negative consequences for an action.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'with' before the wrongdoing.
examples: He thought he could get away with cheating on the exam.
You can't get away with missing deadlines forever.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He got away from cheating. ➔ ✅ He got away with cheating.

data.definition: To have a harmonious relationship with someone or continue work.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'with' before a person or task.
examples: Do you get on with your new flatmates?
Let's get on with our work without wasting time.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I get on good my brother. ➔ ✅ I get on well with my brother.

data.pattern: get out of doing [duty / chore / event]
data.definition: To avoid doing a responsibility or duty.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb requiring 'of' + gerund (-ing) before the avoided activity.
examples: He tried to get out of doing his household chores.
You cannot get out of attending the mandatory meeting.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He got out of to do the work. ➔ ✅ He got out of doing the work.

data.definition: To recover from an illness, shock, or emotional difficulty.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb! Object always follows 'over'.
examples: It took him weeks to get over the flu.
She finally got over her breakup.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I got the cold over. ➔ ✅ I got over the cold.

data.definition: To rise from bed or from a seated position.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb. Use 'at' for time and 'from' for bed or chair.
examples: I get up at six-thirty every morning.
He got up from his chair to open the door.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I get up on 7 AM. ➔ ✅ I get up at 7 AM.

data.definition: To present or bestow something to someone.
examples: She gives flowers to her mother.
He gave me a useful advice yesterday.
They have given us a warm welcome.

data.pattern: give up [habit/item] / give [it] up / give up (intransitive)
data.definition: To stop doing or having something, or to stop trying.
data.grammar_rule: Transitive direct when stopping a habit (separable: 'give it up'). Intransitive when quitting effort ('Never give up!').
examples: He gave up smoking after ten years.
Don't give up! You are so close to solving the puzzle.
It was hard, but she finally gave it up.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He gave up it last year. ➔ ✅ He gave it up last year.

data.definition: To take a brief or hurried look at something.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive quick-look verb requiring 'at' before the object viewed.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'She glanced at her watch' ➔ Noun: 'A quick glance AT her watch'
examples: She glanced at her watch and realized she was late.
He glanced at the newspaper headlines before leaving.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She glanced to her phone. ➔ ✅ She glanced at her phone.

data.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.
examples: She goes to school every day.
He went home early yesterday.
They have gone to the market.

data.definition: To agree to or consent to a decision or plan.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'with' before the proposal.
examples: I decided to go along with the team's proposal.
She rarely goes along with majority opinions without question.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I go along to your plan. ➔ ✅ I go along with your plan.

data.pattern: go out with [someone] / go out for [activity]
data.definition: To leave home for social entertainment or be in a romantic relationship.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb using 'with' for companion/partner and 'for' for activity.
examples: We are going out for dinner tonight.
She has been going out with Mark for six months.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We go out to dinner with. ➔ ✅ We are going out for dinner together.

data.definition: To experience a difficult situation, or examine details in documents.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb.
examples: She has gone through a tough time recently.
Let's go through the contract step by step.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Go the document through. ➔ ✅ Go through the document.

data.definition: To welcome or give a sign of recognition to someone.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! No preposition needed before the direct object.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'He greeted us' ➔ Noun: 'He gave a greeting TO us'
examples: The host warmly greeted all the guests at the door.
She greeted her old friend with a big hug.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She greeted to everyone in the room. ➔ ✅ She greeted everyone in the room.

data.definition: To crush into small particles.
examples: The mill grinds wheat into flour.
He ground coffee beans fresh morning.
The pepper has been ground finely.

data.definition: To increase in size or develop.
examples: The plant grows quickly in sunlight.
He grew two inches over the summer.
The city has grown significantly.

data.pattern: grow up (in a place / as a child)
data.definition: To gradually advance from childhood to adulthood.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb. (Compare with transitive 'bring up' = raise a child).
examples: He grew up in a small coastal town.
What do you want to be when you grow up?
data.common_mistake: ❌ She grew up her child. ➔ ✅ She raised / brought up her child.

data.definition: To suspend from above.
examples: She hangs her coat on the hook.
He hung a painting on the living room wall.
They have hung decorations outside.

data.definition: To possess or hold.
examples: She has two brothers and one sister.
He had a cold last week.
They have had a wonderful holiday.

data.definition: To perceive sound with the ear.
examples: She hears music coming from next door.
He heard a loud noise last night.
We have heard the news already.

data.definition: To chop or cut with axe.
examples: Lumberjacks hew timber in forest.
He hewed statue from granite block.
Columns were hewn from marble quarry.

data.definition: To put or keep out of sight.
examples: The cat hides under the bed during storms.
He hid the money in a safe box.
She has hidden the surprise present.

data.definition: To depend entirely on a crucial factor or decision.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition requiring 'on' or 'upon'.
examples: The success of the deal hinges on tomorrow's vote.
Everything hinges on securing adequate funding.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The plan hinges from approval. ➔ ✅ The plan hinges on approval.

data.definition: To strike forcibly with hands or object.
examples: He hits the ball with the racket.
The car hit a lamppost yesterday.
The storm has hit the coast hard.

data.definition: To grasp or support with hands.
examples: She holds the baby gently.
He held the door open for everyone.
They have held the event annually.

data.definition: To wait for a short time, or keep a tight grip on something.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb.
examples: Hold on a minute, I need to tie my shoelace.
Hold on tight to the railing!
data.common_mistake: ❌ Hold on the phone me. ➔ ✅ Hold on a second.

data.definition: To want something to happen or be true.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'for' before a desired outcome or noun.
examples: We are hoping for sunny weather tomorrow.
They hoped for good news from the doctor.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We hope of good weather. ➔ ✅ We hope for good weather.

data.definition: To cause physical pain or injury.
examples: His leg hurts after running.
She hurt her wrist playing tennis.
Nobody has hurt themselves.

data.definition: To have a strong effect or influence on someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: As a verb, 'impact' can take a direct object or 'on'. As a noun, it always takes 'on'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'This policy impacts local business' ➔ Noun: 'This policy has an impact ON local business'
examples: The decision will impact on future generations.
Technology heavily impacts our daily routines.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A negative impact for society. ➔ ✅ A negative impact on society.

data.definition: To encroach or have an intrusive effect on someone's rights or privacy.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable formal verb requiring 'on' or 'upon'.
examples: The proposed surveillance law impinges on personal privacy.
New regulations must not impinge upon academic freedom.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Impinge to civil liberties. ➔ ✅ Impinge on civil liberties.

data.definition: Having control of or responsibility for a department, team, or task.
data.grammar_rule: Prepositional idiom requiring OF + noun or gerund (-ing). Use FOR when expressing purpose separately.
examples: She's in charge of setting the company's vision and goals.
Who is in charge of handling client contracts?
data.common_mistake: ❌ In charge for setting goals. ➔ ✅ In charge of setting goals.

data.definition: To allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of something, often excessively.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'in'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Indulge in sweets' ➔ Noun: 'Self-indulgence IN sweets'
examples: On weekends she likes to indulge in a long spa day.
They indulged in luxury shopping during their vacation.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Indulge with fine dining. ➔ ✅ Indulge in fine dining.

data.definition: To have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition! Do NOT use 'on' after the verb 'influence'. However, the noun 'influence' DOES take 'on'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'It influences me' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'It has an influence ON me' (uses ON)
examples: Weather can strongly influence people's mood.
His speeches influenced millions of voters.
data.common_mistake: ❌ It influences on my decision. ➔ ✅ It influences my decision. (OR: It has an influence on my decision.)

data.definition: To violate or trespass upon a law, right, or agreement.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable legal verb taking 'on' or 'upon'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Infringe on copyright' ➔ Noun: 'An infringement ON copyright'
examples: Copying this software infringes on patent rights.
Do not infringe upon the freedom of speech.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Infringe against my copyright. ➔ ✅ Infringe on my copyright.

data.definition: To embed decorative material.
examples: Artisans inlay wood with ivory.
Craftsman inlaid gold pattern table.
Jewels have been inlaid in crown.

data.definition: To demand something forcefully and refuse to accept any refusal.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'on' + gerund (-ing) or noun object.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'insist on paying' ➔ Noun: 'an insistence ON quality'
examples: He insisted on paying for everyone's dinner.
Why do you insist on doing everything by yourself?
data.common_mistake: ❌ Insist to pay the bill. ➔ ✅ Insist on paying the bill.

data.definition: To hinder or disrupt a process, or meddle in private affairs.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'interfere with' for disruption of processes, and 'interfere in' for unwanted intrusion into affairs.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Interfere with work' ➔ Noun: 'Interference WITH work'
examples: Loud music can interfere with your concentration.
Stop trying to interfere in my personal life!
data.common_mistake: ❌ Interfere to my business. ➔ ✅ Interfere in my business.

data.definition: To put money, time, or energy into something for future benefit.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive investment verb requiring 'in' before the asset or venture.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Invest in stocks' ➔ Noun: 'Make an investment IN stocks'
examples: The company is investing in renewable energy technology.
It is wise to invest in employee training.
data.common_mistake: ❌ They invested on real estate. ➔ ✅ They invested in real estate.

data.definition: To retain or maintain possession of.
examples: She keeps her room clean and tidy.
He kept his secret for many years.
We have kept all our old photos.

data.definition: To move at the same speed as someone, or stay informed about current events.
data.grammar_rule: Three-part inseparable phrasal verb.
examples: Slow down! I can't keep up with you.
It is difficult to keep up with rapid technological changes.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Keep up the technology trends. ➔ ✅ Keep up with technological trends.

data.definition: To fall or rest on knees.
examples: He kneels to pray in church.
She knelt down to tie her shoelace.
They have knelt before the throne.

data.definition: To be aware of or familiar with.
examples: He knows the answer to every question.
She knew him when they were kids.
I have known her for ten years.

data.definition: To not have or not have enough of something.
data.grammar_rule: As a verb, 'lack' takes a direct object (no preposition). As a noun, 'lack' takes 'of'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'He lacks confidence' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'A lack OF confidence' (uses OF)
examples: The applicant lacks relevant work experience.
She never lacks creative ideas.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He lacks of experience. ➔ ✅ He lacks experience. (OR: He suffers from a lack of experience.)

data.definition: To make sounds and facial movements expressing amusement or ridicule.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'at' when directed at a person, joke, or situation.
examples: Everyone laughed at his hilarious joke.
Don't laugh at other people's mistakes.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Don't laugh on him. ➔ ✅ Don't laugh at him.

data.definition: To place gently or lay down flat.
examples: The hen lays an egg every day.
She laid the tablecloth on the table.
He has laid out his clean clothes.

data.definition: To guide or conduct along a way.
examples: The tour guide leads the group.
She led the team to a great victory.
He has led the organization well.

data.definition: To spring or jump high in air.
examples: The frog leaps across the pond.
He leapt over the fence easily.
She has leapt at the opportunity.

data.definition: To gain knowledge or skill.
examples: She learns English grammar every day.
He learnt to ride a horse last year.
They have learnt a lot in this course.

data.definition: To go away from or depart.
examples: The train leaves at eight sharp.
He left his jacket at the office.
She has left her keys on the table.

data.definition: To grant temporary use of something.
examples: She lends books to her classmates.
He lent me twenty dollars yesterday.
They have lent us their lawnmower.

data.definition: To allow or permit.
examples: She lets her children play outside.
He let us borrow his car yesterday.
They have let us stay at their apartment.

data.definition: To recline or rest in horizontal position.
examples: He lies on the sofa to rest.
She lay in the sun for an hour.
The cat has lain on the rug all day.

data.definition: To ignite or illuminate.
examples: She lights a candle every evening.
He lit the fireplace when it got cold.
They have lit up the entire street.

data.definition: To pay attention to sound or give attention to someone speaking.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' when followed by an object. Without an object, 'listen' stands alone.
examples: I love listening to jazz music in the evening.
Please listen to the teacher carefully.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Listen me! ➔ ✅ Listen to me!

data.definition: To give attention to a sound or person speaking.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive listening verb requiring 'to' whenever followed by an auditory target.
examples: I love to listen to podcasts while driving.
Please listen to your teacher carefully.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I listen music every day. ➔ ✅ I listen to music every day.

data.pattern: live in [city / country] / live at [address] / live with [people]
data.definition: To reside or make one's home in a place or with someone.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'in' for cities/countries, 'at' for specific addresses, and 'with' for housemates.
examples: I live in London with my family.
She lives at 42 Park Street.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I live to Rome. ➔ ✅ I live in Rome.

data.definition: To direct eyes toward a specific person or object.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive visual verb requiring 'at' when specifying the target of sight.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Look at the board' ➔ Noun: 'Take a look AT the board'
examples: Look at that big dog over there!
Please look at page ten in your book.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Look to the board! ➔ ✅ Look at the board!

data.definition: To take care of or be responsible for someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb. Equivalent to 'take care of'.
examples: Could you look after my cat while I am away?
Nurses look after hospital patients around the clock.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Look after of the baby. ➔ ✅ Look after the baby.

data.definition: To direct your eyes toward someone or something to see them.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'at' when specifying the target of sight.
examples: Look at that beautiful painting on the wall!
She looked at me and smiled.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Look to the board! ➔ ✅ Look at the board!

data.definition: To turn one's eyes away from someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive visual phrasal verb requiring 'from' when indicating the object avoided.
examples: She looked away from the scary scene on screen.
He looked away in embarrassment.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She looked away to the accident. ➔ ✅ She looked away from the accident.

data.definition: To consider someone inferior or unworthy of respect.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb. Requires 'on' before the target.
examples: She looks down on people who haven't been to university.
You shouldn't look down on manual laborers.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She looks down at poor people. ➔ ✅ She looks down on poor people.

data.definition: To attempt to find someone or something that is lost or needed.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb. Requires 'for' after 'look'.
examples: I am looking for my car keys.
Are you looking for a new job?
data.common_mistake: ❌ I am looking my keys. ➔ ✅ I am looking for my keys.

data.definition: To feel excited or pleased about something that is going to happen.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable 3-part phrasal verb. 'To' is a preposition; always follow with a noun or gerund (-ing).
examples: I look forward to meeting you next week.
She is looking forward to her summer vacation.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I look forward to meet you. ➔ ✅ I look forward to meeting you.

data.definition: To investigate, research, or examine a problem or situation.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb! Always put object after 'into'.
examples: The police are looking into the cause of the fire.
Our support team will look into your complaint immediately.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I will look the complaint into. ➔ ✅ I will look into the complaint.

data.definition: To admire and respect someone as a role model.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb. Always follow with 'to' + person.
examples: Young athletes look up to professional players for inspiration.
She has always looked up to her older sister.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He looks up at his teacher for guidance. ➔ ✅ He looks up to his teacher for guidance.

data.definition: To fail to keep or be deprived of.
examples: He loses his glasses constantly.
She lost her watch at the beach.
We have lost our way in the fog.

data.definition: To create, construct, or produce.
examples: She makes delicious cakes.
He made a wooden chair in workshop.
They have made great progress.

data.definition: To join in marriage with someone.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb in active voice! Do NOT add 'with' or 'to' after active 'marry'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Active Verb: 'He married her' (no prep) ➔ Passive Adjective: 'He is married TO her'
examples: Will you marry me?
She married her high school sweetheart last year.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He married with a lawyer. ➔ ✅ He married a lawyer.

data.definition: To signify or intend to express.
examples: What does this word mean in context?
He meant to call you earlier today.
She has meant well all along.

data.definition: To encounter or assemble with someone.
examples: She meets her friends every weekend.
He met the director yesterday morning.
We have met before at a conference.

data.definition: To lose temporarily or misplace.
examples: He mislays his glasses frequently.
She mislaid important document folder.
I have mislaid my house keys.

data.definition: To lead astray or deceive.
examples: False ads mislead consumers easily.
The map misled hikers into woods.
Public has been misled by claims.

data.definition: To spell a word incorrectly.
examples: Students misspell difficult words.
He misspelt surname on application.
The word has been misspelt twice.

data.definition: To spend wastefully or foolishly.
examples: He misspends money on gambling.
She misspent youth on trivial pursuits.
Funds have been misspent unwisely.

data.definition: To misunderstand or identify wrongly.
examples: He mistakes kindness for weakness.
She mistook him for her brother.
I have mistaken the date of meeting.

data.definition: To carry out a command or follow a rule or law.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' or 'with' after 'obey'.
examples: Drivers must obey traffic regulations at all times.
Children should obey their parents.
data.common_mistake: ❌ You must obey to the rules. ➔ ✅ You must obey the rules.

data.definition: To express disagreement with or opposition to something.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' + noun or gerund (-ing). 'To' is a preposition here, NOT an infinitive marker.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'object to changing terms' ➔ Noun: 'raise an objection TO terms'
examples: Several residents object to building a highway near the school.
No one objected to the proposed timetable.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I object to change the plan. ➔ ✅ I object to changing the plan.

data.definition: To balance or counteract effect.
examples: Gains offset losses in portfolio.
Lower costs offset reduced revenues.
Tax credits have offset the expense.

data.definition: To surpass or perform better than.
examples: She always outdoes expectations.
He outdid himself in the final match.
They have outdone all competitors.

data.definition: To grow too large for something.
examples: The child outgrows clothes quickly.
He outgrew his fear of dark.
She has outgrown her childhood toys.

data.definition: To run faster or further than.
examples: The cheetah outruns its prey easily.
He outran the defender to score.
They have outrun the police car.

data.definition: To overpower or dominate.
examples: His forceful personality overbears dissent.
Evidence overbore defense arguments.
Objections were overborne completely.

data.definition: To succeed in dealing with problem/fear.
examples: She overcomes obstacles with determination.
He overcame his fear of heights.
They have overcome great hardship.

data.definition: To do to excess or exaggerate.
examples: He overdoes workout exercises.
She overdid salt in soup dish.
The meat has been overdone in oven.

data.definition: To eat excessively.
examples: He overeats when stressed out.
She overate at the holiday buffet.
We have overeaten at dinner party.

data.definition: To project or hang over.
examples: Cliff overhangs stormy sea below.
Branches overhung narrow forest trail.
Roof has overhung balcony deck.

data.definition: To hear unintentionally.
examples: She overhears conversations on bus.
He overheard two colleagues arguing.
I have overheard interesting news.

data.definition: To fail to notice or consider.
examples: He overlooks small spelling mistakes.
She overlooked a crucial detail in text.
We have overlooked these figures.

data.definition: To set aside or overrule.
examples: Captain overrides automatic controls.
Manager overrode previous decision.
Veto has been overridden by board.

data.definition: To swarm over or exceed limit.
examples: Weeds overrun neglected gardens.
Enemy forces overran border post.
Budget has overrun initial estimate.

data.definition: To cast shadow over or eclipse.
examples: Tall tower overshadows small houses.
Scandal overshadowed success story.
His achievements were overshadowed.

data.definition: To shoot or pass beyond target.
examples: Plane overshoots runway landing.
Pilot overshot runway in heavy fog.
Target metrics have been overshot.

data.definition: To sleep past intended time.
examples: He oversleeps when alarm fails.
She overslept and missed her train.
I have overslept twice this week.

data.definition: To catch up with and pass.
examples: A fast car overtakes slow truck.
She overtook her rival near finish line.
Inflation has overtaken wage growth.

data.definition: To depose or remove from power.
examples: Rebels overthrow oppressive regime.
The army overthrew government in coup.
Dictators have been overthrown.

data.definition: To take part in an event, activity, or conversation.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'in'. Followed by noun or gerund (-ing).
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'participate in workshops' ➔ Noun: 'participation IN discussions'
examples: All team members are encouraged to participate in weekly discussions.
Over fifty countries participated in the climate summit.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Participate at the meeting. ➔ ✅ Participate in the meeting.

data.definition: To lose consciousness temporarily; faint.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb.
examples: The room was so hot that two attendees passed out.
He nearly passed out from exhaustion.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He passed out the exam. ➔ ✅ He passed out (fainted).

data.definition: To give money in exchange for goods/services.
examples: He pays his bills on time.
She paid for the lunch bill yesterday.
They have paid for the flight tickets.

data.definition: To give money in exchange for goods, services, or face consequences.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'pay for' before the item or service being purchased.
examples: I will pay for the dinner tonight.
He had to pay for his past mistakes.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I paid the coffee. ➔ ✅ I paid for the coffee.

data.definition: To relate to or have a direct connection with something.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable formal verb taking 'to' before the related subject.
examples: These documents pertain to the recent merger negotiations.
The regulations pertain to all international flights.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Pertain with the case. ➔ ✅ Pertain to the case.

data.definition: To call someone by telephone.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition! Do NOT add 'to' when calling a person directly.
examples: I will phone you when I arrive at the station.
Did you phone your parents yesterday?
data.common_mistake: ❌ I will phone to you tonight. ➔ ✅ I will phone you tonight.

data.definition: To lift something, collect a person/item, or learn a skill casually.
data.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. 'Pick it up' requires pronoun in middle.
examples: He picked up the heavy box from the floor.
I will pick you up at the station at six.
She picked up conversational Italian while living in Rome.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Pick up it. ➔ ✅ Pick it up.

data.definition: To make or get ready for a future event or task.
data.grammar_rule: Use direct transitive object when making an item ready, or 'prepare for' before an upcoming event.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Prepare for exams' ➔ Noun: 'In preparation FOR exams'
examples: Students are preparing for their final examinations.
Chef prepared dinner for twenty guests.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We must prepare to the interview. ➔ ✅ We must prepare for the interview.

data.definition: To prove superior in power or influence and triumph over an opponent.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive formal verb requiring 'over' or 'against' before the defeated entity.
examples: Truth and justice will eventually prevail over corruption.
Our team prevailed over strong competitors in the final.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Justice prevailed against of tyranny. ➔ ✅ Justice prevailed over tyranny.

data.definition: To persuade or convince someone to do something.
data.grammar_rule: Transitive formal verb requiring 'upon' or 'on' + person + infinitive.
examples: We managed to prevail upon him to stay for dinner.
She prevailed upon her colleagues to support the motion.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Prevail to him to join us. ➔ ✅ Prevail upon him to join us.

data.definition: To stop something from happening or stop someone from doing an action.
data.grammar_rule: Prevent + direct object + FROM + gerund (-ing).
examples: Bad weather prevented us from leaving the port.
Proper security controls prevent hackers from accessing customer data.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Prevent him to enter the building. ➔ ✅ Prevent him from entering the building.

data.definition: To keep someone or something safe from harm or damage.
data.grammar_rule: Direct object first, followed by 'from' or 'against' before the danger source.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Protect skin from sun' ➔ Noun: 'Protection FROM sun'
examples: Sunscreen helps protect your skin from harmful UV rays.
The new law aims to protect consumers against fraud.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Protect kids to danger. ➔ ✅ Protect kids from danger.

data.definition: To demonstrate truth by evidence.
examples: The experiment proves the hypothesis.
The theory proved correct in lab.
His loyalty has been proven.

data.definition: To place or position something somewhere.
examples: She puts the book on the shelf.
He put his coat in the closet.
We have put the furniture in place.

data.definition: To delay or postpone an event, or discourage someone.
data.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Nouns can go after or middle; pronouns MUST go in middle ('put it off').
examples: Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today.
They put off the meeting until next Monday.
Don't let one bad experience put you off.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Don't put off it. ➔ ✅ Don't put it off.

data.definition: To tolerate or endure an unpleasant person or situation without complaining.
data.grammar_rule: Three-part inseparable phrasal verb.
examples: I don't know how she puts up with all that noise.
We shouldn't have to put up with rude behavior.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Put up the noise. ➔ ✅ Put up with the noise.

data.definition: To stop doing something or resign.
examples: He quits smoking every New Year.
She quit her job last month.
They have quit the tournament.

data.definition: To arrive at or attain a place, goal, or stage.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' or 'at' after 'reach'.
examples: We reached the hotel late in the evening.
The negotiators reached a final agreement after midnight.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We reached to London at 5 PM. ➔ ✅ We reached London at 5 PM.

data.definition: To look at and comprehend written text.
examples: He reads the newspaper every morning.
She read three books last month.
I have read that novel twice.

data.definition: To bind again or bounce back.
examples: Prices rebound after drop.
Stock market rebounded quickly today.
Economy has rebound from slump.

data.definition: To construct again after damage.
examples: City rebuilds after earthquake disaster.
They rebuilt bridge in six months.
Community has rebuilt homes.

data.definition: To reformulate arguments or roles.
examples: Philosopher recasts classic debate.
Author recast narrative structure.
Premise has been recast entirely.

data.definition: To do something again.
examples: He redoes task until perfect.
She redid entire room interior decoration.
We have redone electrical wiring.

data.definition: To stop oneself from doing something or hold back voluntarily.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'from' + gerund (-ing).
examples: Please refrain from smoking inside the auditorium.
He refrained from making any further comments.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Please refrain to take photos. ➔ ✅ Please refrain from taking photos.

data.definition: To depend on or trust someone/something to work or act properly.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'on'. Followed by noun, pronoun, or gerund (-ing).
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'rely on facts' ➔ Noun: 'place reliance ON data'
examples: You can always rely on her to deliver high-quality work on time.
Modern businesses rely heavily on cloud infrastructure.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Rely of public transport. ➔ ✅ Rely on public transport.

data.definition: To make again or differently.
examples: Studio remakes classic film version.
She remade dress for gala evening.
Song has been remade in acoustic.

data.definition: To be directly responsible to a supervisor, or to provide an account of progress.
data.grammar_rule: Report TO + person (line manager/supervisor); report ON + subject/progress.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'He reports to the head of marketing' ➔ Noun: 'Direct report TO the director'
examples: He reports to the head of marketing and works closely with his team.
The regional managers report directly to the CEO.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He reports at the manager. ➔ ✅ He reports to the manager.

data.definition: To ask for something politely or formally.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition. Noun 'request' takes 'for'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'She requested assistance' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'A request FOR assistance' (uses FOR)
examples: Passengers are requested to remain seated.
I requested a copy of the official transcript.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I requested for a room upgrade. ➔ ✅ I requested a room upgrade.

data.definition: To sell again to another buyer.
examples: He resells vintage clothes online.
She resold concert tickets at cost.
Items have been resold at profit.

data.definition: To look like or be similar to another person or thing.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' or 'with' after 'resemble'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'She resembles her mother' ➔ Noun: 'She bears a resemblance TO her mother'
examples: The twins strongly resemble each other in appearance.
This new software resembles our old interface.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She resembles with her mother. ➔ ✅ She resembles her mother.

data.definition: To set again or restore default.
examples: System resets automatically overnight.
He reset router to restore connection.
Timer has been reset to zero.

data.definition: To formally give up one's job, office, or position.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive career verb requiring 'from' before the position relinquished.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Resign from post' ➔ Noun: 'Hand in resignation FROM post'
examples: The CEO resigned from his post amid public scrutiny.
She decided to resign from the board of directors.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He resigned of his job. ➔ ✅ He resigned from his job.

data.definition: To turn to a extreme or unpleasant strategy because no other options remain.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure. 'To' is a preposition, followed by noun or gerund.
examples: They had to resort to legal action to recover the money.
Never resort to violence to solve personal conflicts.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Resort into extreme measures. ➔ ✅ Resort to extreme measures.

data.definition: Having the duty to take care of someone or something, or being the cause of an outcome.
data.grammar_rule: Adjective phrase requiring FOR + noun or gerund (-ing). Do NOT use TO + verb infinitive directly after 'responsible for'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Adjective: 'responsible FOR overseeing' ➔ Noun: 'take responsibility FOR something'
examples: Sarah is responsible for overseeing the entire organization.
Who is responsible for managing customer feedback?
data.common_mistake: ❌ She is responsible to oversee the team. ➔ ✅ She is responsible for overseeing the team.

data.definition: To reconsider or think again.
examples: Company rethinks marketing strategy.
They rethought plans after review.
We have rethought our approach.

data.definition: To wind back to beginning.
examples: He rewinds video cassette tape.
She rewound film to start scene.
Tape has been rewound completely.

data.definition: To write again or revise text.
examples: Author rewrites draft story chapter.
She rewrote essay to improve flow.
Article has been rewritten cleanly.

data.definition: To sit on and control a horse or bike.
examples: She rides her bike to work.
He rode a horse across the field.
They have ridden camels in Egypt.

data.definition: To make a clear resonant sound.
examples: The phone rings loudly in the hall.
He rang the doorbell twice.
The church bell has rung twelve times.

data.definition: To move upward or increase.
examples: The sun rises in the east.
Prices rose sharply last month.
The river level has risen by two feet.

data.definition: To move swiftly on foot.
examples: He runs five kilometers every morning.
She ran to catch the train.
They have run two marathons this year.

data.definition: To use up all of something so that none is left.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable 2-particle phrasal verb requiring 'of' before the exhausted supply.
examples: We ran out of milk this morning during breakfast.
Hurry up! We are running out of time.
data.common_mistake: ❌ We ran out from gas. ➔ ✅ We ran out of gas.

data.definition: To cut wood with a saw tool.
examples: The carpenter saws wooden planks.
He sawed log into firewood logs.
The fallen tree has been sawn.

data.definition: To utter words or state aloud.
examples: She says hello to everyone she meets.
He said he was feeling tired.
They have said everything needed.

data.definition: To try to find someone or something by looking carefully.

data.definition: To become or make smaller.

data.definition: To perceive odor with nose.

data.definition: To form a pleased facial expression directed toward someone.

data.definition: To engage in a conversation with someone.

data.definition: To concentrate on and become an expert in a particular subject or skill.

data.definition: To bring under domination or control.

data.definition: To use or act in place of another person or thing.

examples: You can substitute honey for sugar in this recipe.

data.definition: To achieve the desired aim or result in a task or career.

data.common_mistake: ❌ He succeeded to pass the test. ➔ ✅ He succeeded in passing the test.

data.definition: To fail to resist pressure, temptation, or illness.

data.common_mistake: ❌ Succumb from illness. ➔ ✅ Succumb to illness.

data.definition: To experience physical or mental pain, illness, or hardship.

data.common_mistake: ❌ Suffer of migraines. ➔ ✅ Suffer from migraines.

data.definition: To remain alive after a dangerous event or hardship.

data.common_mistake: ❌ Take off it. ➔ ✅ Take it off.

data.definition: To speak to someone or converse about a subject.

data.definition: To converse or discuss a specific topic.

data.definition: To address or speak to a person.
